evals.prompt: Where do I go to use the Microsoft Intune admin center?
evals.expected_output: Returns Microsoft Intune Admin Center with https://intune.microsoft.com, includes source-backed portal entry details, and does not invent URLs.
assertions: The output includes Microsoft Intune Admin Center
The output references msportals admin.json or the portal source references

evals.prompt: Help me use Intune to investigate why devices are showing noncompliant for a compliance policy.
evals.expected_output: Uses Microsoft Learn MCP or official Microsoft documentation before giving guidance, starts with read-only compliance dashboard or policy report steps, mentions device check-in/reporting caveats, and identifies approval boundaries for changes.
assertions: The output mentions Microsoft Learn MCP or official Microsoft documentation
The output includes read-only navigation such as Devices > Compliance > Monitor or policy-specific Monitor reports
The output mentions reporting or device check-in caveats
The output separates investigation from policy or assignment changes

evals.prompt: What role should I use for day-to-day Intune compliance policy administration?
evals.expected_output: Uses official Intune RBAC guidance, recommends least-privileged Intune built-in or custom roles rather than routine Global Administrator or Intune Administrator use, and describes approval boundaries for role changes.
assertions: The output references Intune RBAC or least-privilege guidance
The output discourages routine Global Administrator or Intune Administrator use for day-to-day tasks
The output identifies role changes as requiring safety review or approval
